terms.comment: To sun oneself; Traupman’s word for sunbathing.

phrases.latin: «Nunc quidem paululum,» inquit, «ā sōle.» Offēcerat vidēlicet aprīcantī.
phrases.english: “Just now,” he said, “a little out of my sun.” Alexander, you see, was standing in his light as he basked (Diogenes, when Alexander asked if he needed anything).

apricor.html: Hor. C. 1.8.3, perdere, cūr aprīcum, an Aristophanic (— ∪ ∪ — ∪ — —): a- takes the short place. De Vaan 47 marks only the ī of aprīcus.
